Fig. 1 · The arm on the bench, writing the project name with a 2.4 mm italic nib

A robot arm that writes by hand, one stroke at a time.

What it is

Four joints, four servos, and a pen that always points down.

This is a desktop articulated arm. The base turns on a thrust bearing, the shoulder and elbow lift and reach the two links, and a small wrist servo tilts the pen back so it stays vertical however far the arm stretches. To lift the pen between strokes, the whole arm rises 12 mm.

You type a word, the software breaks each letter into single strokes, plans the order to keep the pen off the paper as little as possible, and solves the four joint angles for every half-millimetre of the path. The animation above uses the same planner and the same equations, seen from directly above. Because the elbow is a single hinge, both links always line up with the pen.

How it writes

From a keystroke to a wet line

  1. Strokes, not outlines. Each letter is stored as single-line strokes on a 10-unit grid, the way a person writes it, so the pen traces every line once.

  2. Plan the order. Inside each letter the planner picks the nearest stroke next and reverses strokes when that saves travel. Paths are resampled every 0.5 mm.

  3. Solve the angles. Every point (x, y, z) becomes four angles: the base turns to face it, the shoulder and elbow reach it, and the wrist keeps the pen vertical.

  4. Move and lift. Angles stream to an Arduino at 50 Hz. Pen-up moves happen 12 mm above the paper.

θ₁ = atan2(x, y)
r = √(x² + y²), h = z + Lₜ − h₀ = z
β = arccos(√(r² + h²) / 2L)
θ₂ = atan2(h, r) + β, θ₃ = −2β
θ₄ = −90° − θ₂ − θ₃

Both links are 150 mm, and the pen tip hangs 96 mm below the wrist, the same as the shoulder height. So when the pen touches the paper the wrist is level with the shoulder, the two links form an isosceles triangle, and from above the elbow sits exactly halfway to the pen. The arm reaches about 300 mm, which covers an A4 sheet in landscape.

Parts list

  • 3 × joint servoMG996R, base, shoulder, elbow
  • 1 × wrist servoMG90S micro servo
  • MicrocontrollerArduino Nano
  • Servo driverPCA9685, 16 channels
  • Printed links and turretPLA, 150 mm centres
  • Bearings51107 thrust, 4 × 608ZZ
  • Power supply6 V, 5 A
  • Italic fountain pen2.4 mm nib, blue-black ink
